characters.continuity: DC Comics New 52 (The Flash vol. 4 #30-35 'Out of Time' and The Flash: Futures End #1)
characters.summary: Future Flash is a jaded Barry Allen from about twenty years in the future who travels back in time to change history, killing villains he blames for tragedies in his life and fighting his own younger self to seal a rupture in the Speed Force.

techniques: Lethal super-speed attacks
Flinging objects at super-speed (high-speed rocks)

mechanisms: Speed Force aura shielding him from friction and kinetic impacts (baseline Barry Allen power)
Regenerative healing factor (baseline Barry Allen power)

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
characters.formDifferences: An older, embittered Barry Allen from twenty years ahead who is willing to kill villains (and his own past self) to rewrite the timeline, unlike the present-day Flash.

sources.supports: Baseline Barry Allen powers: Speed Force aura, regenerative healing, time travel via superluminal speed.

Future Flash is a jaded Barry from twenty years in the future; kills Daniel West in The Flash: Futures End #1, cripples his younger self; Wallace West dies in The Flash vol. 4 #35 after being hit by rocks the Future Flash flung.
Future Flash kills Grodd, Reverse-Flash and Mirror Master; seeks to seal a Speed Force rupture by killing his past self.

feats.claim: Travelled back from twenty years in the future and killed Daniel West (Reverse-Flash) to prevent Wallace West's death.
Killed Grodd, Reverse-Flash and Mirror Master, whom he blamed for major tragedies in his life.

notableResults.note: Crippled his younger self in their fight, then disappeared into the past.

unknowns: The exact upper limit of temporal endurance before erasing himself from the timeline.

Correction: Wallace West (Ace West) died in The Flash vol. 4 #35 after shielding the present Flash from high-speed rocks the Future Flash flung, and released Speed Force energy that closed the rupture; no source describes Future Flash disintegrating Wally by molecular vibration.
TV Tropes says Future Flash later sacrifices himself to stop William Selkirk; no opened source records him losing to present-day Barry in The Flash vol. 4 #50, so that result is not recorded.

Removed by review (not supported by any source opened): technique: Cellular molecular vibration disintegration; technique: Speed Force lightning generation; defense: Temporal displacement; weakness: Psychological instability due to trauma and guilt; limitation: Creates catastrophic temporal paradoxes; mobility: Speed Force flight; formDifferences: scarred armored blue-accented suit; feat: Disintegrated Wally West by vibrating his molecules apart; result: loss vs The Flash (Barry Allen) (The Flash vol. 4 #50); conditional: Time travel and timeline erasure; tag: natural-flight (Speed Force hover); tag: self-teleport (time travel by running is not teleportation).

characters.continuity: DC Comics main continuity (post-Crisis New Earth, The Flash vol. 2 era)
characters.summary: Wally West is widely considered the fastest person to hold the title of the Flash, with a mainline connection to the Speed Force that cannot be cut off. He fights by overwhelming opponents with speed, stealing or lending momentum, and phasing through matter.

techniques: Speed steal (absorbing others' speed or momentum)
Lending speed to people or objects
Phasing through solid matter

mechanisms: Speed Force aura protecting him and anyone he carries from the effects of his speed

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
mobility: Dimensional travel (entering the Speed Force by exceeding light speed)
Limited flight by spinning like a helicopter (DC Database, marked citation needed)

sources.supports: Speed Force connection, phasing, protective aura, lending speed, time travel, healing others, outrunning a black hole (The Flash vol. 2 #177).

Powers: mainline Speed Force connection (The Flash vol. 2 #109), phasing, aura, speed steal, time and dimensional travel, regeneration, Anti-Life negation (Final Crisis #4); Mirror Master capture (The Flash vol. 2 #153).
Rogue War: Wally catches Zoom and pushes him into his own sonic boom (The Flash vol. 2 #223).

feats.claim: Outran the gravitational pull of a black hole.
Outran death to the edge of the universe and beyond.
Negated the effects of Darkseid's Anti-Life Equation through physical contact with his Speed Force energy.

notableResults.note: During Rogue War, Wally caught up with Zoom as he attacked Linda and pushed him into his own sonic boom, opening a fissure in time that restored Linda's pregnancy; Wally then brought Zoom back to the present via the cosmic treadmill.
Caught Mirror Master within his speed-stream and hauled him off to prison.

campaignTags.claim: DC Database: Wally could heal from any injury instantly, without prematurely aging.
Wikipedia: by manipulating speed he can boost metabolism so that the recipient rapidly heals from injuries.

unknowns: Exact ceiling of maximum speed when untethered from physical constraints.

Correction: the earlier limitation that he can lose his Speed Force connection is contradicted by DC Database, which says his mainline connection means he cannot be cut off (The Flash vol. 2 #109); removed.
Helicopter-spin flight is listed by DC Database with a citation-needed marker; not tagged pending a better source.

Removed by review (not supported by any source opened): technique: Infinite Mass Punch; technique: Sonic booms; weakness: Vulnerability to absolute zero temperature zones; feat: Infinite Mass Punch leveling a continent-sized threat; feat: Outran instantaneous teleportation across the universe (The Flash vol. 2 #138); result citation The Flash vol. 2 #200 (the opened source places the win in #223); tag: natural-flight (kinetic hover); tag: self-teleport (running across distances is not teleportation).

characters.continuity: DC Comics Rebirth era (Flash Forward 2019-20, The Flash #750, Dark Nights: Death Metal)
characters.summary: After sitting on Metron's Mobius Chair, which had been infused with Doctor Manhattan's power, Wally West gained part of Manhattan's powers and cosmic knowledge on top of his Speed Force connection. He used them to try to restore a fractured timeline; after The Batman Who Laughs took the Chair, he kept only residual Anti-Crisis energy.

techniques: Not established by the cited sources

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
limitations: Without the Mobius Chair he retained only residual Anti-Crisis energy from Doctor Manhattan and was no longer omnipotent (Dark Nights: Death Metal #1).
characters.formDifferences: His costume and lightning turn Manhattan blue with Manhattan's logo on his forehead, and he loses nearly all emotion in favour of logic and knowledge.

sources.supports: The Mobius Chair grants Wally part of Manhattan's powers; in Dark Nights: Death Metal Wally identifies Manhattan's energy, and The Batman Who Laughs takes him prisoner to acquire it.

Chair infused with Manhattan's power (Flash Forward #6); attempt to forge one timeline (Flash Forward #5, The Flash #750); Death Metal #1 loss of the Chair with residual Anti-Crisis energy; time stop with Johnny Quick's Speed Formula (Death Metal #3).
Wally obtains Manhattan's powers; blue costume and lightning, Manhattan logo, loss of emotion; uses the powers to restore the timeline.

feats.claim: Used his Manhattan-enhanced power and cosmic knowledge to try to forge the fragmented timeline into one coherent timeline; the attempt was undone when The Batman Who Laughs corrupted the Multiverse.
Using Johnny Quick's Speed Formula, briefly stopped time during a chase and reached the Mobius Chair.

conditional.dependsOn: Doctor Manhattan's energy infused into the Mobius Chair; after losing the Chair he kept only residual Anti-Crisis energy

unknowns: Full extent of reality manipulation capabilities before the power source dissipates.

This form overlaps with the Mobius Chair Wally West record: the sources describe him gaining Manhattan's power by sitting on the Manhattan-infused Chair. This record covers the Manhattan-powered state, including the post-Chair residual energy in Death Metal.
Doctor Manhattan himself can fly, teleport and change size, but no opened source says which of those powers Wally received, so flight and teleportation are not recorded for this form.

The Darkest Knight 'loss': DC Database says the Darkest Knight had rigged the Mobius Chair to send its energy into himself (Death Metal #4); that was a trap, not a fight, so it is not recorded as a result.

Removed by review (not supported by any source opened): technique: Atomic restructuring; technique: Cosmic energy blasts; technique: Reality warping; defense: Omnidirectional atomic regeneration; defense: Invulnerability to conventional harm; weakness: Mental burden of holding multiversal consciousness; mobility: Flight; mobility: Instantaneous teleportation; feat: Reconstructed the shattered multiverse (the sources describe an attempt that failed); tag: natural-flight; tag: self-teleport.
Extreme or conceptual power scaling: the owner may want to rule on how this form is used in play.

characters.continuity: DC Comics Rebirth era (Flash Forward 2019-20, The Flash #750, Dark Nights: Death Metal)
characters.summary: Seated on Metron's Mobius Chair, Wally West gains near-omniscient sight and understanding of the universe alongside his Speed Force powers. The Chair flies, shields itself with a force field and can carry him through space, time and other dimensions in seconds.

techniques: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: The Chair can be taken from him: The Batman Who Laughs used Perpetua's power to snatch it away (Dark Nights: Death Metal).
mobility: Teleportation through space, time and other dimensions via the Chair
characters.formDifferences: Seated on the Mobius Chair, which grants near-omniscient sight; Wally is the only known being not fully overtaken by the Chair (The Flash #750).

sources.supports: Wally sits on the Mobius Chair (Flash Forward #6), surveys the timeline (Flash Forward #5, The Flash #750); The Batman Who Laughs, empowered by Perpetua, defeats him and strips him of the Chair (Dark Nights: Death Metal #1).
Mobius Chair abilities: flight, teleportation through space, time and dimensions, near-omniscience, force field; Wally as its host.
Wally, trying to fix reality by merging timelines, is stopped by The Batman Who Laughs, who used Perpetua's power to snatch away the Mobius Chair.
Wally finds Metron's Mobius Chair and gains cosmic knowledge (Flash Forward).

feats.claim: Took possession of the Mobius Chair's knowledge and surveyed the whole timeline, finding repeated events.

notableResults.note: The Batman Who Laughs, empowered by Perpetua, defeated Wally and stripped him of the Mobius Chair.

conditional.ability: Near-omniscience and teleportation through space, time and dimensions
conditional.dependsOn: Being seated on the Mobius Chair

campaignTags.claim: The Mobius Chair's main capability is to travel and teleport through space, time and other dimensions in seconds.

unknowns: Whether Wally could permanently separate from the chair without catastrophic backlash.
Correction: the continuity was given as Dark Nights: Metal / Justice League; the sources place Wally's time on the Chair in Flash Forward, The Flash #750 and Dark Nights: Death Metal.
Correction: the 'loss vs Perpetua' result is recorded as a loss to The Batman Who Laughs, who used Perpetua's power to take the Chair.

Removed by review (not supported by any source opened): technique: Mobius beam energy projection; technique: Information overload; defense: Impenetrable divine energy shield of the New Gods; defense: Temporal displacement immunity; weakness: Vulnerability to mental corruption from absorbing infinite universal data; formDifferences: anti-matter propulsion; feat: Scanned every timeline and piece of knowledge in existence simultaneously; tag: natural-flight (Chair flight is a device, so it is tagged powered-flight).
Extreme or conceptual power scaling: the owner may want to rule on how this form is used in play.
Unsupported by cited source (term check, 0/5 key terms found): powered-flight: DC Database's Mobius Chair page says the Chair can also fly; Wally flies by riding it.

characters.continuity: DC Comics main continuity (Golden Age through Prime Earth; hosts Jim Corrigan and Crispus Allen)
characters.summary: The Spectre is God's spirit of vengeance bound to a human host, with near-omnipotent magical and physical power over space, time, reality and matter. He punishes the wicked with reality-warping transformations, but is bound by the Presence's laws and needs a human host to stay stable.

techniques: Reality warping and transformation of victims (e.g. into broken glass or melting candles)
Illusions and hallucinations
Possessing objects and intruding on minds or souls

weaknesses: The Spear of Destiny can kill him
Soulless beings such as Nekron are immune to his powers (Green Lantern #51, 2010)
Libra was unaffected by his powers (Final Crisis: Revelations)
limitations: Needs a human host to keep his power in check; without one the Spectre-Force becomes unstable and rampages
Bound by divine laws and tasks set by the Presence

sources.supports: Powers (near-omnipotence, magic, reality warping, flight, intangibility), host dependence, Presence's laws, weaknesses, More Fun #52, Adventure Comics #431-440, Day of Vengeance, Eclipso in Justice League of America #57 (2011).
Prime Earth Spectre: strongest of the Judge class, bound to host Corrigan, limited by The Voice's tasks.
Crisis on Infinite Earths #10: a magically empowered Spectre creates an energy overload that shatters space and time and merges the five Earths.

feats.claim: His touch instantly reduced a murderer to a skeleton.
Transformed criminals into broken glass and melting candles.
Magically empowered by the assembled heroes, created an energy overload that shattered space and time while the Anti-Monitor waited at the dawn of time; the five Earths merged into one universe.

notableResults.note: Under Jean Loring's manipulation, turned the Phantom Stranger into a mouse.
Killed Shazam while manipulated by Jean Loring.
Eclipso cleaved him in two and absorbed his power.

campaignTags.claim: Wikipedia lists flight among the Spectre's innate supernatural powers.
Wikipedia describes near-omnipotent magical abilities and energy and magic manipulation.

unknowns: The absolute extent of his power if operating completely free of a host constraint.
Crisis on Infinite Earths: Wikipedia says he is the only hero who can stand against the Anti-Monitor directly, but no opened source states the outcome of their clash, so no result is recorded.

Removed by review (not supported by any source opened): technique: Size manipulation; technique: Divine judgment bolts; technique: Soul tearing; defense: Divine invulnerability; defense: Conceptual immortality; mobility: Teleportation; mobility: Dimensional travel; feat: Turned a man into a living salt crystal and moved the Earth's orbit (More Fun Comics #52 is a different feat); tag: self-teleport; tag: giant-sized (no documented size in an opened source); tag: spellcaster (replaced by magic).

conquest of worlds and dimensions

characters.continuity: DC Comics main continuity (Golden Age Detective Comics through post-Crisis and Modern Age)
characters.summary: Harvey Dent, formerly Gotham's District Attorney, is Two-Face, a crime boss obsessed with duality who lets a scarred double-headed coin decide his actions. He has no superpowers and relies on marksmanship, martial arts, heavy firearms and his legal knowledge to plan number-two themed crimes.

techniques: Dual-pistol marksmanship
Heavy weapons (Tommy guns, shotguns, grenade and rocket launchers)
Martial arts improved by Deathstroke and Batman
Bombs (detonated a bomb in his apartment to escape Batman)

mechanisms: Criminal planning informed by knowledge of criminal law and police procedure

weaknesses: Total reliance on his scarred double-headed coin to make decisions

sources.supports: Skills, weapons, coin, number-two crimes, Face the Face, Batman #234 and #258, Detective Comics #513, Long Halloween-era capture.

feats.claim: Re-scarred his face with nitric acid and a scalpel to return as Two-Face, threatened the Gotham Zoo and detonated a bomb in his apartment to escape Batman's questioning.

notableResults.note: Knocked unconscious by Batman.
Batman foiled Two-Face's plan.
Took revenge on Falcone, Fields and Maroni but was captured by Batman.
After Batman escaped Two-Face's trap, Robin stopped Two-Face.

unknowns: Whether psychological rehabilitation can permanently suppress the Two-Face persona.
The DC Database page (dc.fandom.com/wiki/Harvey_Dent_(Prime_Earth)) failed to load, so it was dropped from sources; the record now rests on Wikipedia.

Correction: Detective Comics #80 ('The End of Two-Face') is the story where Harvey is cured by plastic surgery; no opened source supports Gemini's claim that Batman beat him there by exploiting the coin.

Removed by review (not supported by any source opened): technique: Explosive coin traps; technique: Gangland tactical ambushes; defense: Body armor; defense: Fortified hideouts; mobility: Automobiles; feat: Took over multiple Gotham crime families through coordinated assassinations (Batman: The Long Halloween); result: loss vs Batman (Detective Comics #80); tag: gadgets (rigged coins are not documented; firearms are not gadgets).

characters.continuity: DC Comics main continuity (post-Crisis New Earth through Rebirth/Prime Earth)
characters.summary: Mari Jiwe McCabe wears the Tantu Totem, created by the trickster god Anansi, which links her to the Red (Earth's morphogenetic field) so she can take on the attributes of animals, one at a time. She is also a skilled hand-to-hand fighter.

techniques: Animal attribute mimicry through the Tantu Totem
Hand-to-hand combat
Matching and draining the abilities of those around her (Justice League of America vol. 2 era)

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Losing the Tantu Totem disconnects her from the Red; Maksai's theft and the Grundy/Amazo plot both exploited this
Can be brainwashed (Gorilla Grodd did so at least once)
Animal instincts can override her control
mobility: Animal-derived movement (depends on the animal mimicked)
limitations: Takes on the attributes of one animal at a time
Her powers are weaker without the Tantu Totem

sources.supports: Tantu Totem created by Anansi and linked to Earth's morphogenetic field; one animal at a time; reduced powers without it; Amazo, General Maksai, Grodd.
Prime Earth: limited powers without the totem; fought Doctor Manhattan on Mars; defeated Doctor Hate with Deadeye.

notableResults.note: Maksai, transformed into a raging beast, died in battle with Vixen.
Vixen and several teammates were beaten into unconsciousness by Amazo.
Prime Earth: one of the heroes who confronted him on Mars and were easily defeated.
Prime Earth: with Deadeye and other heroes in the Congo; she cut him off from the Kingdom without harming it.

characters.continuity: DC Comics main continuity (post-Crisis New Earth through Prime Earth/Rebirth)
characters.summary: Diana of Themyscira is an Amazon warrior princess with god-given strength, speed and flight, wielding the Lasso of Truth, nearly indestructible bracelets and a Hephaestus-forged sword. She fights hand-to-hand and deflects bullets and energy blasts with her bracelets.

techniques: Hephaestus-forged sword strikes
Lasso of Truth binding
Deflecting bullets and energy blasts with her bracelets

mechanisms: Nearly indestructible bracelets of Eighth Metal
Highly resistant to concussive force and extreme temperatures (not invulnerable)
Accelerated healing while in contact with the Earth

weaknesses: Edged weapons and projectiles with enough force can pierce her skin
Grail's Omega Beams can shatter her bracelets
Aphrodite's Law (Golden Age): if a man chains her bracelets she loses her Amazon strength
limitations: Her accelerated healing depends on contact with the Earth

sources.supports: Powers (Hermes' flight and speed, strength, healing, durability), equipment, weaknesses, Maxwell Lord (Wonder Woman vol. 2 #219), Neron, Circe, Nubia.
Flight from Hermes, bracelets that deflect Darkseid's Omega Beams, Hephaestus-forged sword, fights with Ares and Darkseid.
Lasso forged by Hephaestus from the Golden Girdle of Gaea; mystical in origin.

feats.claim: Her Bracelets of Submission, of nearly indestructible Eighth Metal, can deflect even Darkseid's Omega Beams.
Can fly at speeds approaching half the speed of light.

notableResults.note: Broke free of a mind-controlled Superman by slicing his throat with her tiara, then snapped Lord's neck after the lasso revealed only death would stop him.
Prime Earth: impaled Ares and the First Born with a spear; Ares died.
Destroyed him from inside by calling out her half-siblings' spirits; he re-emerged elsewhere.
After Circe reverted her to clay, Diana was revived and defeated Circe with Donna Troy.
Neron killed Diana in battle; the Olympian gods then granted her divinity.
Their duel ended in a draw.

campaignTags.claim: Hermes granted Diana superhuman speed and the ability to fly.
Her Lasso of Truth, forged by Hephaestus from the Golden Girdle of Gaea, is mystical in origin.

unknowns: Exact limits of her divine combat potential when removing her limiter bracelets.
After the 2011 relaunch she lost natural flight and regained it only after a feather thrown by Hermes struck her (per Wikipedia).

Removed by review (not supported by any source opened): technique name 'God Killer' (the source describes a Hephaestus-forged sword without that name); feat: exchanged blows with Superman that shattered tectonic plates; result: inconclusive vs Superman; feat citation Wonder Woman (vol. 2) #170 for bracelet deflection (the deflection is sourced without an issue).

characters.continuity: Flashpoint Timeline (DC Comics Flashpoint, 2011; later The Button)

She rules New Themyscira, the former United Kingdom, with her Female Furies, and killed Mera in retribution.

techniques: Not established by the cited sources

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
characters.formDifferences: A warlord Diana who rules New Themyscira (the former United Kingdom) with her Female Furies and wages the Amazon-Atlantean war that devastated western Europe, unlike prime Diana.

sources.supports: War between Wonder Woman and Aquaman decimated western Europe; she fights Aquaman one-on-one until Flash's team arrives (Flashpoint #4).
War began with Hippolyta's death at the wedding, engineered by Penthesilea and Orm; Diana rules New Themyscira, the former United Kingdom, with her Female Furies.
Wonder Woman killed Mera in retribution; their final battle was interrupted by the Flash and the heroes.

feats.claim: Rules New Themyscira, the former United Kingdom, with the aid of her Female Furies.
Killed Mera in retribution for Hippolyta's death.

notableResults.note: They fought one-on-one until the Flash and his team arrived to stop the war; the timeline was later restored by the Flash.

unknowns: Whether her power differs fundamentally from prime Diana outside of psychological disposition.
